title: No Verified Case Can Support Dog-Trade Defenses
excerpt: No police record, court judgment, seizure, or health alert is documented here. Honest reform needs proof, quarantine, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
No verified police seizure, court judgment, transport interception, poison-bait incident, or emergency health alert appears in available records. That absence cannot defend dog meat trade. It blocks honest storytelling—and exposes why transparent enforcement matters.

Tradition Cannot Replace Traceability

Claims about “farm-raised dogs,” stolen companions, or illicit transport require named cases, dates, locations, agency records, and court documents. None are documented here. No honest campaign should turn an unverified claim into a crime scene.

Biosecurity Still Demands Control

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters wounds, broken skin, or mucous membranes through bites or scratches. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. See World Health Organization rabies guidance.

Household exposure and commercial animal transport are separate biosecurity questions. Neither permits invented causal links. Both require quarantine, inspection, traceability, and accountable enforcement.

Demand Proof. Demand Protection.

Vietnamese families and communities deserve protection from theft, unsafe handling, and preventable disease risk. SDE’s demand goes beyond unverified claims: complete abolition of dog meat trade by 2030, backed by transparent enforcement and public accountability. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action—and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.

No verified case can defend dog-trade claims.

• Available records document no named police seizure, court judgment, transport interception, poison-bait incident, or emergency health alert.
• Claims about stolen pets, “farm-raised dogs,” and illicit networks need dates, locations, agencies, and court records.
• Rabies exposure involves infected saliva entering bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes—not properly cooked meat.
• Wash possible exposure with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek urgent medical care. PEP must start before symptoms. Rabies is virtually 100% fatal after symptoms appear.
• Household exposure and commercial transport remain separate biosecurity questions. Quarantine, inspection, and traceability protect communities.

SDE demands complete abolition of dog meat trade by 2030, with transparent enforcement. Sign the petition: https://c.org/nLZTZdVNdJ
